concerns.text: Task T103 (Contract validation of all result artifacts) is placed **before** T104 (Run‑book reconciliation and pipeline orchestration). Validation consumes artifacts that the orchestrator (T104) (re)creates, so the consumer runs before the producer, violating data‑flow ordering.

Task T109 (Circularity check) is scheduled after many downstream tasks (e.g., T104, T108). The circularity check must run **before** model training/scaffold split (T027) and before the orchestrator, otherwise a circular model could be trained and only aborted later, breaking the producer‑before‑consumer rule.

Task T104 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it orchestrates the entire workflow, writing and overwriting many artifacts (descriptors, model_output, plots, etc.). Such a monolithic script cannot be safely run in parallel with other `[P]` tasks; the `[P]` tag is therefore inaccurate.

Task T103 is also marked `[P]` yet it reads artifacts that T104 later overwrites. Running T103 in parallel with T104 could lead to race conditions and validation of stale files, so the `[P]` designation is unsafe.

Task T108 (Feature/VIF JSON report) is marked `[P]` but depends on the output of T102 (permutation importance) and T039 (VIF calculation). If executed in parallel before those producers finish, it would generate an incomplete report. The `[P]` tag should be removed or the task reordered after its producers.
